bugs.text: Script throws at load: `SPR.chal=[mkSprite(SPR.zako[0]?undefined:undefined)]` passes undefined to mkSprite, which reads rows[0].length. A leftover line that line 189 immediately overwrites. Everything after it (input, state, loop) never runs, so the page is a blank black canvas; nothing responds to keys.

P.cd is never initialised, so `P.cd<=0` is `undefined<=0` = false: the player can never fire a shot, even if the load crash were fixed. Shots fired, hits, dual-fighter shots and all enemy kills by the player are impossible.

G.mode is never set to 'challenge'; beginStage always goes intro -> play. On stages 3, 7, 11... no entry queue is built, no enemy appears, and after 70 ticks the stage is skipped. Challenging stages, their scoring and the NUMBER OF HITS screen never happen.
Stage badge denominations are 50/20/10/5/1; the arcade's 30 badge is missing.
sTracTick is called every tick for 210 ticks while the beam is on, creating 210 oscillators; a buzzy, overlapping tractor sound rather than a tone.

Formation enemies never fire on stage 1 (`G.stage>1` gate) and the dive fire gate at 403 is per-tick random, so some dives fire many aimed bullets in a row; the in-formation firing itself is non-arcade behaviour.
Dead/unreachable code left in: mkFlag with a bogus palette map, `e.state==='captive'&&false`, and a self-assigning beamBoss expression.

summary: The source reads like a competent, compact Galaga: well-sectioned state/update/render, Bezier entry and dive paths in five groups of eight, a correct 4/16/20 formation with sway and breathing, escorted boss dives with 400/800/1600 scoring, a working-looking tractor-beam capture, rescue, dual fighter and hostile captive, seven synthesized sounds, READY respawn gating, and tight hitboxes. None of it runs. A stray debugging line (188) passes undefined into the sprite builder and the script dies before the key handlers, game state or animation loop are even defined, leaving a blank black canvas; the play-test shows no title, no start and no movement. Two further defects would surface the moment that line was deleted: the player can never fire because P.cd is never initialised, and challenging stages are silently skipped because the 'challenge' mode is never entered. So in delivered form it is a well-structured but unverified draft rather than a game, and its faithfulness to Galaga can only be read from dead code.
